author: NASASpaceflight
description:
A four-tonne Falcon 9 second stage has crashed into the Moon—but despite the dramatic headlines, was the impact actually a big deal?

This week, we examine how often objects of this size naturally strike the lunar surface, what astronomers observed during the Falcon 9 impact, and whether uncontrolled rocket-stage crashes could become a concern as humanity prepares to establish a permanent presence on the Moon.

We also cover major updates across the spaceflight industry:

• NASA reveals new progress on Artemis III, Artemis IV, Orion, SLS, and its future Moon Base
• Blue Origin narrows down the cause of New Glenn’s explosion
• Blue Moon Mark 1 prepares for its first lunar mission
• Relativity Space completes structural qualification testing of Terran R’s first stage
• Rocket Lab reveals new details about Neutron and its “Hungry Hippo” fairing
• ULA prepares Vulcan and the new Centaur V configuration for testing
• NASA sets a launch date for SpaceX Crew-13
